clue.text: Fine material for painting a coat in the desert

definitions.meaning: fine artists' brushes are traditionally made from the soft fur of a desert pack animal
the shaggy fleece worn by the dromedary or Bactrian beast of the sands

explanation.surface: An artist hunts for fine paint while wearing a jacket out in the Sahara.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushes and woollen cloth are both made from the fur of a desert animal, which is also that animal's natural coat.

clue.text: Not at home with a certain style

definitions.meaning: out, elsewhere, as a team playing on the opponents' ground
read as two words, 'a way' of doing something is a manner

explanation.surface: Someone is out of the house and dressed with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means absent from one's house, and split in two it names a manner or method.

clue.text: Tire out at the back of the car

definitions.meaning: to wear out or drain someone completely

definitions.text: at the back of the car
definitions.meaning: the pipe at a vehicle's rear that carries fumes away

explanation.surface: A long drive leaves someone worn out, with fumes coming from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means drain of energy, and the noun is the tailpipe system venting a motor's spent gases.

clue.text: It can't report M Ps who are C

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'It can't report M Ps who are C', is garbled: 'C' cannot be read, so the cryptic sense of the clue is missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: It can't report M Ps who are C

clue.text: I circle West Africa where some Sioux Indians survive

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
WA is the abbreviation for West Africa

explanation.surface: Someone traces a ring round a map of West Africa, then wonders about Native American tribes.
explanation.walkthrough: The state takes its name from a Siouan-speaking people, who still live there.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state is named after a Siouan tribe still living in the region.

clue.text: Crude share-out for four in slum property

definitions.meaning: dividing something carelessly into four portions gives uneven fourths
poor, run-down lodgings or a dangerous part of town

explanation.surface: Four people split a run-down house badly between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the phrase is an uneven split into fourths; as an idiom it means squalid lodgings.

clue.text: Terrorised by a silencer?

parts.note: a silencer suggests a gun, but here it is anyone who frightens a person out of saying anything

explanation.surface: A victim is menaced by a gunman's muffled pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silencer' points at a gun, but the clue means someone so frightened they dare not utter a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too scared to open their mouth has been silenced by fear.

clue.text: Tittle about Nathan's wife endless; created ridicule in the deanery

indicators.note: the word for a tittle goes round the other pieces, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: a tittle is a tiny amount, as is a jot
taken as written, the possessive giving its S

indicators.note: the wife loses her final letter, the word having no end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman's title surrounds the endless story of Nathan's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The satirist of Gulliver's Travels was Dean of St Patrick's, Dublin, hence 'the deanery'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish satirist wrote his mockery while serving as a cathedral dean in Dublin.

clue.text: It accommodates members after a round or two, perhaps

definitions.text: It accommodates members after a round or two, perhaps

parts.words: It accommodates members after a round or two, perhaps
parts.note: a round of golf, after which club members gather in their building for a drink

explanation.surface: A pub welcomes regulars after they have bought a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a round' suggests drinks, but it is a round of golf and the members are of a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf club members retire to their pavilion once they finish playing.

clue.text: Boss leading the way into a dive

parts.note: the boss is the head of an organisation
being in front, at the start

explanation.surface: A manager sets an example by plunging into a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver going in head-down plunges with the top of the body leading.

clue.text: Was it used to pull Eskimos first?

definitions.text: Was it used to pull Eskimos first?

parts.note: to lug is to haul or drag

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Eskimos is wanted

explanation.surface: A question about whether Arctic peoples were dragged on a small sled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer, a small sled.
explanation.definitionFit: A small toboggan is the sort of vehicle one might picture hauling Arctic travellers.

clue.text: Claud reformed with grace

indicators.note: the name Claud is formed again into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Claud mends his ways and behaves gracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: A duke is addressed as 'Your Grace', so the adjective for a duke means 'with grace'.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is styled His Grace, so something befitting a duke goes with that title.

clue.text: Turn deaf and pale

indicators.note: turn tells us the letters of deaf are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone loses their hearing and goes white.
explanation.definitionFit: To pale is to lose colour, to grow dim or weaker.

clue.text: Dove-shaped fantail across the Tamar

indicators.note: the letters of Dove are shaped into a different arrangement

parts.note: read as fan-tail, the last letter of fan

explanation.surface: A pigeon breed with a fan-shaped tail flies over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantail' is a pigeon breed alongside 'Dove', but split it gives the tail of 'fan'. The River Tamar divides Cornwall from the English county to its east.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county lies on the far bank of the Tamar when seen from Cornwall.

clue.text: Top chefs are fond of a spicy oil it yields

indicators.note: the top of chefs is its opening letter

parts.note: to be fond of something is to love it

explanation.surface: Leading cooks are keen on a particular aromatic oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried flower bud of this spice is distilled into a pungent oil used in cooking and dentistry.

clue.text: A gift one leaves behind in advance?

definitions.text: A gift one leaves behind in advance?

parts.words: A gift one leaves behind in advance?
parts.note: a present arranged ahead of time, to be handed over when the giver has left this life

explanation.surface: Someone drops off a present early before departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves behind' means bequeaths on death; 'in advance' because a will sets it out before then.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something left to others by will, arranged before one dies.

clue.text: Misguided lord of the court caught in the act

indicators.note: the judge's address is held inside the word for an act

parts.note: a deed is an act
barristers address a judge as 'm'lud', so lud is the lord of the court

explanation.surface: A judge is caught red-handed doing something foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in the act' reads as one idiom, but 'caught in' is the container signal and 'act' alone is the outer word; 'm'lud' is how English barristers address a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deceived into wrong beliefs has been misled.

clue.text: The eloquent language of the chapel?

definitions.meaning: the art of public speaking, fine rhetoric
a small place of private prayer

explanation.surface: A preacher's fine speech echoes through a small church.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means skilful rhetoric and also names a small place set apart for prayer.

clue.text: It describes a possession on which you are solitary

definitions.text: It describes a possession on which you are solitary

parts.words: It describes a possession on which you are solitary
parts.note: the phrase marks something as belonging to the person addressed, and put after 'on' it means alone

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about property and loneliness.
explanation.walkthrough: Something belonging to you is described with this phrase, and 'on' it you are by yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase marks belonging to the reader, and with 'on' before it, being alone.

clue.text: Italian consumer groups may accept such cases

definitions.text: Italian consumer groups may accept such cases

parts.words: Italian consumer groups may accept such cases
parts.note: consumer groups taking on complaints, but really diners in Italy eating little stuffed pasta parcels

explanation.surface: Consumer organisations in Italy take on complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' suggests legal complaints, but here they are pasta parcels with a filling, and the 'consumers' are eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: These small filled pasta squares are cases of dough that Italian diners consume.

clue.text: How the world gets through its daily round

definitions.text: How the world gets through its daily round

parts.words: How the world gets through its daily round
parts.note: the Earth spins on its axis once each day

explanation.surface: A remark on how everyone copes with their routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the world' sounds like everybody, but it is the planet, spinning once a day.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet turns on its axis once every twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Locate ground for construction

definitions.meaning: a plot of land where building takes place

explanation.surface: A developer finds a plot to build on.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means position, and the noun is a plot set aside for building.

clue.text: Springfield's 24?

definitions.meaning: the first name of the British pop singer Springfield
points to the clue at 24-down, whose answer means covered in a fine grey powder

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to a singer and another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the stage first name of the 1960s singer Springfield and also means powdery, like ash.

clue.text: Father caught in ends of mattress springs

indicators.note: the word for father is held within the outer letters
the end of the word mattress is its closing pair of letters, the double S

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Dad gets trapped among the coils of a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'springs' looks like part of the mattress, but it is the definition: places with mineral springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorts built around mineral springs are named after these healing waters.

clue.text: A shot at describing 1666 London?

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as in a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A gunshot fired at the city in the year of the plague.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Fire of London in 1666 left the city covered in cinders.
explanation.definitionFit: After the Great Fire the city was covered in cinders and grey residue.

clue.text: Examination for dentistry?

parts.note: a spoken test, and dentists deal with the mouth

explanation.surface: A student sits a test to become a dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: A spoken exam is named from the mouth, the part dentists examine.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test is named from the mouth, which is a dentist's field.

clue.text: Recurrence of a cheeky attack?

parts.note: fresh can mean impudent or forward
a sudden attack of illness or violence is an outbreak

explanation.surface: Someone suffers another bout of impudent behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something breaking out again is a renewed occurrence.

clue.text: Beside a singular dwarf there's nobody else

parts.note: by means next to
a can mean one
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
an elf is a small mythical being like a dwarf

explanation.surface: A lone little man stands with nobody else around.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone means no other person is present.
